reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: All 3 gates passed. Gate 1 skipped (missing-validation finding — the issue is absent RLS enforcement, not a dead function; getMembersData is actively called at page.tsx:68). Gate 2: no trust_assumptions defined in BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json; attack vector is an untrusted authenticated user calling Supabase REST API directly. Gate 3: src/app/dashboard/ and src/lib/supabase/ are explicitly in scope. Verdict is CONFIRMED_POTENTIAL because the attack path is plausible (anon key is publicly visible in the client bundle; any authenticated user can supply their session JWT directly to Supabase REST API, bypassing the Next.js admin layout guard entirely and receiving all members' records), but exploitability depends on the actual Supabase RLS policy — no SQL schema files exist in the repository to confirm whether USING clause is permissive (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL) or admin-restricted. The codebase pattern of app-layer-only enforcement across all 11 RPC functions and the use of createClient() (not createAdminClient()) for the members SELECT strengthens the likelihood of a permissive RLS policy.
